findings.claim: EIA storage releases are information events for natural-gas futures: volatility rises around the release and prices respond to unexpected storage changes.
findings.expected_direction: positive inventory surprise -> lower futures price, all else equal

findings.claim: Natural-gas futures exhibit a distinct announcement-day return pattern: more than half of annual return was earned on EIA storage-announcement days in the published sample, and the announcement-versus-non-announcement difference was not explained by storage surprise or standard controls.
findings.expected_direction: announcement-day return distribution differs from non-announcement days

findings.claim: Natural-gas futures react materially less to EIA inventory announcements released on Fridays than on Thursdays; 2026 evidence estimates a 74% weaker daily response on Friday.
findings.expected_direction: Friday-shifted release -> weaker response than normal Thursday release

findings.claim: Trader positioning may contain incremental information, but the literature base does not justify assuming it is a dominant Henry Hub driver relative to physical fundamentals.
findings.expected_direction: incremental effect must be demonstrated after physical controls
